q18471.en: Driving lanes are part of the carriageway.

explain.short: Driving lanes are where vehicles move, so they are inside the carriageway (carreggiata).
explain.rule: The carreggiata (carriageway) is where vehicles move: lanes and crossings are inside it. Verges, sidewalks and emergency lanes are outside it.
explain.trap: 'corsie di marcia' are the normal driving lanes, the heart of the carriageway.

sceneParams.caption: Driving lanes are inside the carriageway

q18472.en: Cycle crossings are part of the carriageway.

explain.short: A cycle crossing is painted across the road where vehicles drive, so it lies on the carriageway.
explain.rule: The carreggiata (carriageway) is where vehicles move: lanes and crossings are inside it. Verges, sidewalks and emergency lanes are outside it.
explain.trap: 'attraversamenti' are crossings drawn ON the road surface, so they are inside the carriageway, even if bikes use them.

sceneParams.caption: Cycle crossings are painted on the carriageway

q18473.en: Pedestrian crossings are part of the carriageway.

explain.short: A pedestrian crossing (zebra crossing) is painted on the carriageway itself, where cars drive.
explain.rule: The carreggiata (carriageway) is where vehicles move: lanes and crossings are inside it. Verges, sidewalks and emergency lanes are outside it.
explain.trap: 'attraversamenti pedonali' are for pedestrians, but they are drawn ON the carriageway.

sceneParams.caption: Zebra crossings are painted on the carriageway

q18474.en: Overtaking lanes are part of the carriageway.

explain.short: An overtaking lane is a lane where vehicles move, so it is inside the carriageway.
explain.rule: The carreggiata (carriageway) is where vehicles move: lanes and crossings are inside it. Verges, sidewalks and emergency lanes are outside it.
explain.trap: 'corsie di sorpasso' are still lanes, and every lane belongs to the carriageway.

sceneParams.caption: Overtaking lanes are inside the carriageway

q18475.en: Motorway emergency lanes are part of the carriageway.

explain.short: The motorway emergency lane runs next to the carriageway, outside it. It is only for stopping in an emergency.
explain.rule: The carreggiata (carriageway) is where vehicles move: lanes and crossings are inside it. Verges, sidewalks and emergency lanes are outside it.
explain.trap: 'corsie' makes it sound like a driving lane, but the emergency lane is outside the carriageway.

sceneParams.caption: The emergency lane is next to, not in, the carriageway

q18476.en: Verges are part of the carriageway.

explain.short: The banchina (verge) is beside the carriageway, beyond the white edge line. It is part of the road, but not of the carriageway.
explain.rule: The carreggiata (carriageway) is where vehicles move: lanes and crossings are inside it. Verges, sidewalks and emergency lanes are outside it.
explain.trap: 'banchine' belong to the road (strada), not to the carriageway (carreggiata).

sceneParams.caption: The verge is outside the carriageway

q18477.en: Sidewalks are part of the carriageway.

explain.short: The marciapiede (sidewalk) is for pedestrians and lies outside the carriageway, where vehicles do not drive.
explain.rule: The carreggiata (carriageway) is where vehicles move: lanes and crossings are inside it. Verges, sidewalks and emergency lanes are outside it.
explain.trap: 'marciapiedi' are part of the road (strada), but not of the carriageway.

sceneParams.caption: The sidewalk is outside the carriageway

q18478.en: A lane can be intended for the normal movement of vehicles.

explain.short: Most lanes are just normal driving lanes, used by vehicles going along the road.
explain.rule: A corsia (lane) is a part of the carriageway for one single line of vehicles. It can be for normal driving, overtaking, accelerating, slowing down, turning, emergencies or reserved vehicles.
explain.trap: 'può essere' (can be) is correct: normal driving is one of the possible uses of a lane.

sceneParams.caption: Normal lanes carry ordinary traffic

q18479.en: A lane is bounded by solid or dashed lines.

explain.short: Lanes are marked on the road surface with white lines, which can be solid or dashed.
explain.rule: A corsia (lane) is a part of the carriageway for one single line of vehicles. It can be for normal driving, overtaking, accelerating, slowing down, turning, emergencies or reserved vehicles.
explain.trap: 'continue o discontinue': both kinds of line can mark a lane.

sceneParams.caption: Lanes are marked by solid or dashed lines

q18480.en: A lane can be an acceleration lane.

explain.short: An acceleration lane is a special lane to pick up speed before joining a fast road.
explain.rule: A corsia (lane) is a part of the carriageway for one single line of vehicles. It can be for normal driving, overtaking, accelerating, slowing down, turning, emergencies or reserved vehicles.
explain.trap: 'può essere' (can be): acceleration is one of the special uses of a lane.

sceneParams.caption: An acceleration lane is a special lane

q18481.en: A lane can be a deceleration lane.

explain.short: A deceleration lane is a special lane to slow down when you leave a fast road.
explain.rule: A corsia (lane) is a part of the carriageway for one single line of vehicles. It can be for normal driving, overtaking, accelerating, slowing down, turning, emergencies or reserved vehicles.
explain.trap: 'può essere' (can be): slowing down is one of the special uses of a lane.

sceneParams.caption: A deceleration lane is a special lane

q18482.en: Lanes can be forbidden to certain types of vehicles.

explain.short: Signs can ban some vehicles from a lane, for example lorries from the left lane of a motorway.
explain.rule: A corsia (lane) is a part of the carriageway for one single line of vehicles. It can be for normal driving, overtaking, accelerating, slowing down, turning, emergencies or reserved vehicles.
explain.trap: 'vietate' (forbidden): a lane can be closed to some vehicles, not to all.

sceneParams.caption: Some lanes are closed to some vehicles

q18483.en: A lane can be reserved for the traffic of some categories of vehicles (taxis, buses, etc.).

explain.short: Bus lanes and taxi lanes are lanes reserved for some categories of vehicles.
explain.rule: A corsia (lane) is a part of the carriageway for one single line of vehicles. It can be for normal driving, overtaking, accelerating, slowing down, turning, emergencies or reserved vehicles.
explain.trap: 'riservata' (reserved): only the listed vehicles may use it.

sceneParams.caption: Bus and taxi lanes are reserved lanes

q18484.en: A lane can be intended for overtaking.

explain.short: On roads with more lanes in the same direction, the left lane is used for overtaking.
explain.rule: A corsia (lane) is a part of the carriageway for one single line of vehicles. It can be for normal driving, overtaking, accelerating, slowing down, turning, emergencies or reserved vehicles.
explain.trap: 'effettuare sorpassi' (to overtake): overtaking is one of the uses of a lane.

sceneParams.caption: An overtaking lane is a type of lane

q18485.en: The road owner can require that, on a lane, vehicles travel at a compulsory minimum speed.

explain.short: The road owner (ente proprietario) can set a minimum speed on a lane, shown by a round blue sign, so slow vehicles stay out of it.
explain.rule: A corsia (lane) is a part of the carriageway for one single line of vehicles. It can be for normal driving, overtaking, accelerating, slowing down, turning, emergencies or reserved vehicles.
explain.trap: 'velocità minima obbligatoria' (compulsory minimum speed) really exists: there are minimum limits, not only maximum ones.

sceneParams.caption: A lane can have a compulsory minimum speed

q18486.en: A lane is a part of the carriageway that allows the traffic of a single line of vehicles.

explain.short: This is the definition of a lane: a strip of the carriageway wide enough for one line of vehicles.
explain.rule: A corsia (lane) is a part of the carriageway for one single line of vehicles. It can be for normal driving, overtaking, accelerating, slowing down, turning, emergencies or reserved vehicles.
explain.trap: 'una sola fila' (one single line) is the key of the definition.

sceneParams.caption: One lane = one single line of vehicles

q18487.en: A lane can be intended for emergency stops, in case of breakdown or illness.

explain.short: The emergency lane (corsia di emergenza) is a lane for stopping only when you have a breakdown or feel ill.
explain.rule: A corsia (lane) is a part of the carriageway for one single line of vehicles. It can be for normal driving, overtaking, accelerating, slowing down, turning, emergencies or reserved vehicles.
explain.trap: 'soste di emergenza' (emergency stops): only real emergencies, not normal parking.

sceneParams.caption: The emergency lane is for breakdowns and illness

q18488.en: A lane can be reserved for vehicles that intend to turn (specialised lane).

explain.short: Before junctions there are often lanes only for vehicles turning left or right: these are specialised lanes.
explain.rule: A corsia (lane) is a part of the carriageway for one single line of vehicles. It can be for normal driving, overtaking, accelerating, slowing down, turning, emergencies or reserved vehicles.
explain.trap: 'corsia specializzata' (specialised lane) is a lane with a specific job, such as turning.

sceneParams.caption: Turning lanes are specialised lanes

q18489.en: A lane can be intended for slowing down vehicles leaving the motorway.

explain.short: This is the deceleration lane: you move into it and slow down when you leave the motorway.
explain.rule: A corsia (lane) is a part of the carriageway for one single line of vehicles. It can be for normal driving, overtaking, accelerating, slowing down, turning, emergencies or reserved vehicles.
explain.trap: 'rallentamento' (slowing down) describes the deceleration lane.

sceneParams.caption: The deceleration lane is for slowing down

q18490.en: A lane is intended only for pedestrians.

explain.short: A lane is part of the carriageway and is for vehicles. Pedestrians walk on sidewalks.
explain.rule: A corsia (lane) is a part of the carriageway for one single line of vehicles. It can be for normal driving, overtaking, accelerating, slowing down, turning, emergencies or reserved vehicles.
explain.trap: 'solo' (only) and 'pedoni' (pedestrians) make it wrong: lanes are for vehicles.

sceneParams.caption: Lanes are for vehicles, not only for pedestrians

explain.short: A lane takes one line of vehicles going in one direction. A road or carriageway can be two-way, a single lane cannot.
explain.rule: A corsia (lane) is a part of the carriageway for one single line of vehicles. It can be for normal driving, overtaking, accelerating, slowing down, turning, emergencies or reserved vehicles.
explain.trap: 'doppio senso' (two-way) belongs to a road or carriageway, never to one single lane.

sceneParams.caption: One lane = one direction only

q18492.en: A lane is a track reserved for racing cars.

explain.short: A lane is a normal part of the carriageway for everyday traffic. It has nothing to do with racing.
explain.rule: A corsia (lane) is a part of the carriageway for one single line of vehicles. It can be for normal driving, overtaking, accelerating, slowing down, turning, emergencies or reserved vehicles.
explain.trap: 'corsia' sounds like 'corsa' (race), but it means a traffic lane.

sceneParams.caption: A lane is for normal traffic, not racing

q18493.en: A lane can never be crossed by pedestrians.

explain.short: Pedestrians cross lanes all the time at pedestrian crossings, which are on the carriageway.
explain.rule: A corsia (lane) is a part of the carriageway for one single line of vehicles. It can be for normal driving, overtaking, accelerating, slowing down, turning, emergencies or reserved vehicles.
explain.trap: 'mai' (never) is too strong: pedestrians may cross, especially at crossings.

sceneParams.caption: Pedestrians do cross lanes at crossings

q18494.en: A lane is made up of two carriageways.

explain.short: It is the other way round: a carriageway is made of one or more lanes.
explain.rule: A corsia (lane) is a part of the carriageway for one single line of vehicles. It can be for normal driving, overtaking, accelerating, slowing down, turning, emergencies or reserved vehicles.
explain.trap: 'formata da due carreggiate' turns the order upside down.

sceneParams.caption: The carriageway is made of lanes, not the opposite

q18495.en: A lane is a fast-flowing road.

explain.short: A lane is only a strip of the carriageway, not a whole road.
explain.rule: A corsia (lane) is a part of the carriageway for one single line of vehicles. It can be for normal driving, overtaking, accelerating, slowing down, turning, emergencies or reserved vehicles.
explain.trap: 'strada a scorrimento veloce' is a type of road, not a lane.

sceneParams.caption: A lane is a strip, not a whole road

q18496.en: In built-up areas, two motorcycles can ride side by side in the same lane.

explain.short: A lane takes only one line of vehicles, so two motorcycles must ride one behind the other.
explain.rule: A corsia (lane) is a part of the carriageway for one single line of vehicles. It can be for normal driving, overtaking, accelerating, slowing down, turning, emergencies or reserved vehicles.
explain.trap: 'Nei centri abitati' (in built-up areas) changes nothing: never two side by side in one lane.

sceneParams.caption: One lane: motorbikes go in single file

q18497.en: Outside built-up areas, two mopeds can ride side by side in the same lane.

explain.short: A lane takes only one line of vehicles, and mopeds must always ride in single file.
explain.rule: A corsia (lane) is a part of the carriageway for one single line of vehicles. It can be for normal driving, overtaking, accelerating, slowing down, turning, emergencies or reserved vehicles.
explain.trap: 'Fuori dai centri abitati' (outside built-up areas) changes nothing: mopeds never ride side by side.

sceneParams.caption: Mopeds always ride in single file

q18498.en: The acceleration lane makes it easier for vehicles to enter the motorway or main extra-urban roads.

explain.short: In the acceleration lane you reach the speed of the traffic, so you can join the fast road safely.
explain.rule: The acceleration lane lets you pick up speed to join a motorway or main extra-urban road. It is not for overtaking.
explain.trap: 'facilita l'ingresso' (makes entry easier): it is about ENTERING, not leaving.

sceneParams.caption: Acceleration lane: entering fast roads

q18499.en: The acceleration lane is for entering the motorway correctly.

explain.short: You use the acceleration lane to join the motorway at the right speed, without slowing the traffic.
explain.rule: The acceleration lane lets you pick up speed to join a motorway or main extra-urban road. It is not for overtaking.
explain.trap: 'entrare' (to enter) is the right purpose of this lane.

sceneParams.caption: Acceleration lane: join the motorway correctly

q18500.en: The acceleration lane is used to increase speed.

explain.short: That is what its name says: you accelerate in it to reach the speed of the traffic.
explain.rule: The acceleration lane lets you pick up speed to join a motorway or main extra-urban road. It is not for overtaking.
explain.trap: 'aumentare la velocità' (increase speed) is exactly what 'accelerazione' means.

sceneParams.caption: You speed up in the acceleration lane

q18501.en: The acceleration lane is for getting back onto the motorway carriageway after leaving a service area.

explain.short: When you leave a service area you use an acceleration lane to rejoin the motorway traffic.
explain.rule: The acceleration lane lets you pick up speed to join a motorway or main extra-urban road. It is not for overtaking.
explain.trap: 'rientrare' (to get back in) means entering again, so the acceleration lane is right.

sceneParams.caption: From the service area back onto the motorway

q18502.en: The acceleration lane can be used for overtaking.

explain.short: The acceleration lane is only for picking up speed and joining the traffic. Overtaking in it is forbidden.
explain.rule: The acceleration lane lets you pick up speed to join a motorway or main extra-urban road. It is not for overtaking.
explain.trap: 'sorpasso' (overtaking) is the wrong use: you only accelerate and merge.

sceneParams.caption: No overtaking in the acceleration lane

q18503.en: The acceleration lane is for leaving a lay-by.

explain.short: A piazzola (small lay-by) is a short stopping place at the side of the road; acceleration lanes are for joining motorways and main roads.
explain.rule: The acceleration lane lets you pick up speed to join a motorway or main extra-urban road. It is not for overtaking.
explain.trap: 'piazzola di sosta' (lay-by) is not where acceleration lanes are used.

sceneParams.caption: Acceleration lanes join fast roads, not lay-bys

q18504.en: The acceleration lane is for leaving the motorway carriageway and entering a rest area.

explain.short: Leaving the motorway to enter a rest area uses the DEceleration lane. The acceleration lane is for joining the motorway.
explain.rule: The acceleration lane lets you pick up speed to join a motorway or main extra-urban road. It is not for overtaking.
explain.trap: 'abbandonare' (to leave) describes the deceleration lane, not the acceleration lane.

sceneParams.caption: To leave the motorway you use the deceleration lane

q18505.en: The deceleration lane makes it easier for vehicles to leave the motorway.

explain.short: You move into the deceleration lane and slow down there, without braking in the fast traffic.
explain.rule: The deceleration lane lets you leave a motorway or main extra-urban road and slow down outside the traffic. You must not stop on it.
explain.trap: 'uscita' (exit, leaving): the deceleration lane is for going OUT.

sceneParams.caption: Deceleration lane: leaving the motorway

q18506.en: The deceleration lane is for leaving a main extra-urban road correctly.

explain.short: Main extra-urban roads also have deceleration lanes at their exits, so you can slow down safely.
explain.rule: The deceleration lane lets you leave a motorway or main extra-urban road and slow down outside the traffic. You must not stop on it.
explain.trap: 'strada extraurbana principale' (main extra-urban road) has them too, not only motorways.

sceneParams.caption: Main roads also have deceleration lanes

q18507.en: The deceleration lane is for leaving the motorway carriageway and entering the service area.

explain.short: To enter a service area you leave the motorway, so you use the deceleration lane and slow down there.
explain.rule: The deceleration lane lets you leave a motorway or main extra-urban road and slow down outside the traffic. You must not stop on it.
explain.trap: 'uscire ... ed entrare nell'area di servizio': you exit the motorway first, so it is deceleration.

sceneParams.caption: Into the service area via the deceleration lane

q18508.en: The deceleration lane can be used for parking vehicles.

explain.short: The deceleration lane is only for slowing down and exiting. Stopping or parking on it is forbidden.
explain.rule: The deceleration lane lets you leave a motorway or main extra-urban road and slow down outside the traffic. You must not stop on it.
explain.trap: 'sosta' (parking) is never allowed in this lane.

sceneParams.caption: No parking in the deceleration lane

q18509.en: The deceleration lane is for entering a lay-by.

explain.short: A piazzola (small lay-by) is reached directly from the road, without a deceleration lane. Deceleration lanes lead to exits and service areas.
explain.rule: The deceleration lane lets you leave a motorway or main extra-urban road and slow down outside the traffic. You must not stop on it.
explain.trap: 'piazzola di sosta' (lay-by) is the wrong place: deceleration lanes lead to exits.

sceneParams.caption: Deceleration lanes lead to exits, not lay-bys

q18510.en: The deceleration lane is for entering the motorway.

explain.short: To enter a motorway you need to speed up, so you use the ACceleration lane, not the deceleration lane.
explain.rule: The deceleration lane lets you leave a motorway or main extra-urban road and slow down outside the traffic. You must not stop on it.
explain.trap: 'entrare' (to enter) belongs to the acceleration lane.

sceneParams.caption: To enter you use the acceleration lane

q18511.en: As a rule, the verge does not allow vehicles to drive on it.

explain.short: The banchina (verge) is outside the carriageway: normally vehicles do not drive there.
explain.rule: The banchina (verge) is part of the road outside the carriageway, beyond the solid white edge line. As a rule vehicles do not drive on it.
explain.trap: 'di norma' (as a rule): you may use it only in special cases, like an emergency stop.

sceneParams.caption: As a rule, no driving on the verge

q18512.en: The verge is a part of the road located outside the carriageway.

explain.short: The verge belongs to the road (strada), but it lies outside the carriageway where vehicles move.
explain.rule: The banchina (verge) is part of the road outside the carriageway, beyond the solid white edge line. As a rule vehicles do not drive on it.
explain.trap: 'strada' and 'carreggiata' are different: the verge is in the first, not in the second.

sceneParams.caption: The verge is part of the road, outside the carriageway

q18513.en: The verge is a part of the road located beyond the solid white edge line of the carriageway.

explain.short: The solid white edge line marks where the carriageway ends; the verge is on the other side of it.
explain.rule: The banchina (verge) is part of the road outside the carriageway, beyond the solid white edge line. As a rule vehicles do not drive on it.
explain.trap: 'oltre' (beyond) is right: the verge starts after the edge line.

sceneParams.caption: The verge is beyond the solid white edge line

q18514.en: The verge is reserved for slow vehicles on uphill roads.

explain.short: Slow vehicles on climbs use a special lane on the carriageway. The verge is not for driving.
explain.rule: The banchina (verge) is part of the road outside the carriageway, beyond the solid white edge line. As a rule vehicles do not drive on it.
explain.trap: 'riservata ai veicoli lenti' (reserved for slow vehicles) describes a lane, not the verge.

sceneParams.caption: Slow vehicles don't drive on the verge

q18515.en: On verges, parking of vehicles is allowed for up to 5 hours.

explain.short: There is no 5-hour parking rule for verges: this number is invented by the quiz.
explain.rule: The banchina (verge) is part of the road outside the carriageway, beyond the solid white edge line. As a rule vehicles do not drive on it.
explain.trap: 'massimo di 5 ore' (up to 5 hours) is a made-up time limit.

sceneParams.caption: No 5-hour parking rule on verges

q18516.en: The verge divides the carriageway into two lanes.

explain.short: Lanes are divided by white lines on the carriageway. The verge is at the side, outside the carriageway.
explain.rule: The banchina (verge) is part of the road outside the carriageway, beyond the solid white edge line. As a rule vehicles do not drive on it.
explain.trap: 'divide la carreggiata' is wrong: the verge is beside the carriageway, not in the middle.

sceneParams.caption: The verge is at the side, not in the middle

q18517.en: The verge is part of the carriageway, intended for parking vehicles.

explain.short: The verge is outside the carriageway, and it is not a parking area.
explain.rule: The banchina (verge) is part of the road outside the carriageway, beyond the solid white edge line. As a rule vehicles do not drive on it.
explain.trap: 'parte della carreggiata' is wrong: the verge is part of the road, outside the carriageway.

sceneParams.caption: The verge is not part of the carriageway

q18518.en: The sidewalk is a part of the road, raised or marked off in another way, reserved for pedestrians.

explain.short: This is the definition of a sidewalk: a raised or separated strip of the road for people on foot.
explain.rule: The marciapiede (sidewalk) is outside the carriageway and reserved, as a rule, for pedestrians. Parking on it is allowed only with special parking lines.
explain.trap: 'rialzata o delimitata in altro modo': a sidewalk does not have to be raised.

sceneParams.caption: Sidewalk: raised or marked off, for pedestrians

q18519.en: The sidewalk is a part of the road reserved, as a rule, for pedestrians.

explain.short: The sidewalk is for people on foot. Vehicles may use it only in special cases, like marked parking.
explain.rule: The marciapiede (sidewalk) is outside the carriageway and reserved, as a rule, for pedestrians. Parking on it is allowed only with special parking lines.
explain.trap: 'di norma' (as a rule) leaves room for exceptions, such as parking lines.

sceneParams.caption: Sidewalks are, as a rule, for pedestrians

q18520.en: The sidewalk allows vehicles to park only where there are special parking lines.

explain.short: Parking on a sidewalk is forbidden, unless parking spaces are painted there.
explain.rule: The marciapiede (sidewalk) is outside the carriageway and reserved, as a rule, for pedestrians. Parking on it is allowed only with special parking lines.
explain.trap: 'solo' (only) is right here: without the lines you may not park on the sidewalk.

sceneParams.caption: Park on a sidewalk only inside painted bays

q18521.en: The sidewalk is a part of the road, outside the carriageway, intended for pedestrian traffic.

explain.short: The sidewalk is part of the road but outside the carriageway, and it is for people on foot.
explain.rule: The marciapiede (sidewalk) is outside the carriageway and reserved, as a rule, for pedestrians. Parking on it is allowed only with special parking lines.
explain.trap: 'al di fuori della carreggiata' (outside the carriageway) is the key point.

sceneParams.caption: Sidewalk: outside the carriageway, for walkers

q18522.en: The sidewalk is a part of the carriageway.

explain.short: The sidewalk is part of the road (strada), but it is outside the carriageway.
explain.rule: The marciapiede (sidewalk) is outside the carriageway and reserved, as a rule, for pedestrians. Parking on it is allowed only with special parking lines.
explain.trap: 'carreggiata' is the trap: the sidewalk belongs to the road, not to the carriageway.

sceneParams.caption: The sidewalk is outside the carriageway

q18523.en: The sidewalk is a part of the road reserved also for bicycles.

explain.short: The sidewalk is reserved for pedestrians. Bicycles use the carriageway or cycle paths.
explain.rule: The marciapiede (sidewalk) is outside the carriageway and reserved, as a rule, for pedestrians. Parking on it is allowed only with special parking lines.
explain.trap: 'anche alle biciclette' (also for bicycles) is wrong: only pedestrians.

sceneParams.caption: Bicycles don't ride on the sidewalk

q18524.en: The sidewalk is reserved for pedestrians and parked vehicles, if it is not raised.

explain.short: A sidewalk is for pedestrians whether it is raised or not. Parked vehicles are allowed only with special parking lines.
explain.rule: The marciapiede (sidewalk) is outside the carriageway and reserved, as a rule, for pedestrians. Parking on it is allowed only with special parking lines.
explain.trap: 'qualora non sia rialzato' (if it is not raised) is an invented condition.

sceneParams.caption: Raised or not, the sidewalk is for pedestrians

q18525.en: The sidewalk is a part of the road where, as a rule, mopeds may park.

explain.short: As a rule only pedestrians use the sidewalk. Mopeds may not park there unless there are parking lines.
explain.rule: The marciapiede (sidewalk) is outside the carriageway and reserved, as a rule, for pedestrians. Parking on it is allowed only with special parking lines.
explain.trap: 'ciclomotori' (mopeds) are vehicles: they follow the same parking ban on sidewalks.

sceneParams.caption: No parking for mopeds on the sidewalk

q18526.en: The pedestrian island, placed at pedestrian crossings, also serves as shelter or a waiting place for pedestrians crossing the road.

explain.short: On a wide road, pedestrians can stop safely on the island halfway across.
explain.rule: The salvagente (pedestrian island) is a safe area for pedestrians at crossings and at tram or bus stops. It may have posts with fixed yellow lights.
explain.trap: 'anche' (also): the island also helps at crossings, not only at tram and bus stops.

sceneParams.caption: Pedestrians wait safely halfway across

q18527.en: The pedestrian island makes it easier for passengers to get on and off trams, trolleybuses or buses.

explain.short: At stops in the middle of the road, passengers wait and get on or off from the island, away from traffic.
explain.rule: The salvagente (pedestrian island) is a safe area for pedestrians at crossings and at tram or bus stops. It may have posts with fixed yellow lights.
explain.trap: 'salita e discesa' (getting on and off): this is the main job of the island at stops.

sceneParams.caption: Passengers board trams from the island

q18528.en: The pedestrian island can be marked by lit posts with a fixed yellow light.

explain.short: To be seen well, especially at night, the island can have small posts with a steady yellow light.
explain.rule: The salvagente (pedestrian island) is a safe area for pedestrians at crossings and at tram or bus stops. It may have posts with fixed yellow lights.
explain.trap: 'luce gialla fissa' (fixed yellow light): steady, not flashing.

sceneParams.caption: Island posts can have a fixed yellow light

q18529.en: The pedestrian island serves to divide the directions of traffic on a two-way road.

explain.short: Separating the two directions is the job of a central divider (spartitraffico). The island is for pedestrians.
explain.rule: The salvagente (pedestrian island) is a safe area for pedestrians at crossings and at tram or bus stops. It may have posts with fixed yellow lights.
explain.trap: 'dividere i sensi di marcia' describes the spartitraffico, not the salvagente.

sceneParams.caption: The island is for pedestrians, not for splitting traffic

q18530.en: The pedestrian island serves to channel vehicles in various directions.

explain.short: Channelling vehicles is the job of traffic islands for vehicles. The salvagente protects pedestrians.
explain.rule: The salvagente (pedestrian island) is a safe area for pedestrians at crossings and at tram or bus stops. It may have posts with fixed yellow lights.
explain.trap: 'incanalare i veicoli' (channel vehicles) is about cars, while the salvagente is about pedestrians.

sceneParams.caption: The island protects pedestrians, it doesn't steer cars

q18531.en: The pedestrian island is a person in charge of first aid.

explain.short: In traffic law the salvagente is a place in the road, not a person.
explain.rule: The salvagente (pedestrian island) is a safe area for pedestrians at crossings and at tram or bus stops. It may have posts with fixed yellow lights.
explain.trap: 'salvagente' also means lifebuoy in everyday Italian, but here it is a pedestrian island.

sceneParams.caption: Salvagente is a place, not a person

q18532.en: The pedestrian island is a cycle and pedestrian route.

explain.short: The salvagente is a small safe area in the road, not a route for bikes and walkers.
explain.rule: The salvagente (pedestrian island) is a safe area for pedestrians at crossings and at tram or bus stops. It may have posts with fixed yellow lights.
explain.trap: 'itinerario ciclopedonale' (cycle-pedestrian route) is a different road type.

sceneParams.caption: Salvagente is a waiting spot, not a route

q18533.en: The driveway entrance lets vehicles reach private properties beside the road (garages, courtyards, etc.).

explain.short: A passo carrabile is the opening where cars go from the road into a garage or courtyard.
explain.rule: A passo carrabile (driveway entrance) is where vehicles enter private side areas. You may stop briefly (fermata) in front of it, but not park (sosta).
explain.trap: 'proprietà private' (private properties): it is an access, not a road or a car park.

sceneParams.caption: A driveway leads into garages and courtyards

q18534.en: The driveway entrance lets vehicles travelling on a public road reach a side area used for parking.

explain.short: A driveway can also lead from the road into a side area where vehicles park.
explain.rule: A passo carrabile (driveway entrance) is where vehicles enter private side areas. You may stop briefly (fermata) in front of it, but not park (sosta).
explain.trap: 'area laterale adibita alla sosta' (side parking area): the parking is inside, not in front of the driveway.

sceneParams.caption: A driveway can lead into a parking area

q18535.en: The driveway entrance must have a special sign showing the authority and the authorisation number.

explain.short: A real passo carrabile has an official sign with the name of the authority (ente) and the permit number.
explain.rule: A passo carrabile (driveway entrance) is where vehicles enter private side areas. You may stop briefly (fermata) in front of it, but not park (sosta).
explain.trap: 'deve' (must): without this sign it is not an official driveway.

sceneParams.caption: Driveway sign: authority + permit number

q18536.en: The driveway entrance is an area for vehicles to access properties beside the road.

explain.short: This is the definition: a place where vehicles go in and out of side properties.
explain.rule: A passo carrabile (driveway entrance) is where vehicles enter private side areas. You may stop briefly (fermata) in front of it, but not park (sosta).
explain.trap: 'accesso' (access) is the key word of the definition.

sceneParams.caption: Driveway = access to side properties

q18537.en: In front of the driveway entrance, stopping is allowed.

explain.short: A fermata (short stop, driver ready to leave) does not block the driveway for long, so it is allowed.
explain.rule: A passo carrabile (driveway entrance) is where vehicles enter private side areas. You may stop briefly (fermata) in front of it, but not park (sosta).
explain.trap: 'fermata' (short stop) is allowed; 'sosta' (parking) is not.

sceneParams.caption: Short stop in front of a driveway: allowed

q18538.en: The driveway entrance is a park-and-ride car park.

explain.short: A park-and-ride is a car park where you leave the car and take public transport. A driveway is only an access.
explain.rule: A passo carrabile (driveway entrance) is where vehicles enter private side areas. You may stop briefly (fermata) in front of it, but not park (sosta).
explain.trap: 'parcheggio scambiatore' (park-and-ride) has nothing to do with a driveway.

sceneParams.caption: A driveway is an access, not a car park

q18539.en: The driveway entrance is a road reserved for animal-drawn carts.

explain.short: 'carrabile' comes from 'carro' (cart), but today it just means vehicles can pass. It is an access, not a road.
explain.rule: A passo carrabile (driveway entrance) is where vehicles enter private side areas. You may stop briefly (fermata) in front of it, but not park (sosta).
explain.trap: 'carri trainati da animali' plays on the old word 'carro'.

sceneParams.caption: A driveway is an access, not a road for carts

q18540.en: The driveway entrance is a road reserved for lorries.

explain.short: A driveway is an access to private properties for any vehicle, not a road for lorries.
explain.rule: A passo carrabile (driveway entrance) is where vehicles enter private side areas. You may stop briefly (fermata) in front of it, but not park (sosta).
explain.trap: 'riservata agli autocarri' (reserved for lorries) is invented.

sceneParams.caption: A driveway is an access for any vehicle

q18541.en: The driveway entrance is a round pedestrian island.

explain.short: A pedestrian island is a salvagente. A driveway is a vehicle access to private properties.
explain.rule: A passo carrabile (driveway entrance) is where vehicles enter private side areas. You may stop briefly (fermata) in front of it, but not park (sosta).
explain.trap: 'salvagente circolare' mixes up two different road parts.

sceneParams.caption: A driveway is not a pedestrian island

q18542.en: The driveway entrance is a sign that requires roundabout traffic around a square.

explain.short: A driveway is a place (an access to properties), not a roundabout sign.
explain.rule: A passo carrabile (driveway entrance) is where vehicles enter private side areas. You may stop briefly (fermata) in front of it, but not park (sosta).
explain.trap: 'segnale che impone la circolazione rotatoria' describes a roundabout sign.

sceneParams.caption: A driveway is an access, not a roundabout sign

q18543.en: In front of the driveway entrance, parking is allowed.

explain.short: Parking (sosta) in front of a driveway would block the way in and out, so it is forbidden.
explain.rule: A passo carrabile (driveway entrance) is where vehicles enter private side areas. You may stop briefly (fermata) in front of it, but not park (sosta).
explain.trap: 'sosta' (parking) is forbidden; only a 'fermata' (short stop) is allowed.

sceneParams.caption: No parking in front of a driveway

q18544.en: Two-wheeled vehicles with a combustion engine up to 50 cm3 and a top speed of 45 km/h are mopeds.

explain.short: This matches the definition of a ciclomotore: two wheels, combustion engine up to 50 cm3, top speed 45 km/h.
explain.rule: A ciclomotore (moped) has 2 or 3 wheels, a top speed of 45 km/h and, with a combustion engine, at most 50 cm3. First test after 4 years, then every 2 years.
explain.trap: 'fino a 50' and '45 km/h' are the exact limits: above them it is a motorcycle.

sceneParams.caption: Up to 50 cm3 and 45 km/h = moped

q18545.en: Mopeds can have two or three wheels.

explain.short: There are two-wheeled mopeds and three-wheeled mopeds: both are ciclomotori.
explain.rule: A ciclomotore (moped) has 2 or 3 wheels, a top speed of 45 km/h and, with a combustion engine, at most 50 cm3. First test after 4 years, then every 2 years.
explain.trap: 'due o tre ruote' is correct: three-wheelers can be mopeds too.

sceneParams.caption: Mopeds: two or three wheels

q18546.en: Not all two-wheeled motor vehicles are classed as mopeds.

explain.short: Bigger or faster two-wheelers (over 50 cm3 or over 45 km/h) are motorcycles (motocicli), not mopeds.
explain.rule: A ciclomotore (moped) has 2 or 3 wheels, a top speed of 45 km/h and, with a combustion engine, at most 50 cm3. First test after 4 years, then every 2 years.
explain.trap: 'Non tutti' (not all) is right: some are mopeds, others are motorcycles.

sceneParams.caption: Bigger two-wheelers are motorcycles

keywords.it: veicoli a motore a due ruote

q18547.en: Two-wheeled mopeds cannot have a combustion engine of more than 50 cm3.

explain.short: 50 cm3 is the maximum engine size of a two-wheeled moped with a combustion engine.
explain.rule: A ciclomotore (moped) has 2 or 3 wheels, a top speed of 45 km/h and, with a combustion engine, at most 50 cm3. First test after 4 years, then every 2 years.
explain.trap: 'superiore a 50' (more than 50): above 50 cm3 it is no longer a moped.

sceneParams.caption: Two-wheeled moped: max 50 cm3

q18548.en: Mopeds must be tested four years after first registration, and then every two years.

explain.short: Like cars, mopeds need a roadworthiness test (revisione): the first after 4 years, then every 2 years.
explain.rule: A ciclomotore (moped) has 2 or 3 wheels, a top speed of 45 km/h and, with a combustion engine, at most 50 cm3. First test after 4 years, then every 2 years.
explain.trap: 'quattro' then 'due': the same timing as cars.

sceneParams.caption: Moped test: after 4 years, then every 2

q18549.en: Mopeds do not have more than two wheels.

explain.short: Mopeds can also have three wheels, so 'not more than two' is wrong.
explain.rule: A ciclomotore (moped) has 2 or 3 wheels, a top speed of 45 km/h and, with a combustion engine, at most 50 cm3. First test after 4 years, then every 2 years.
explain.trap: 'non hanno più di due ruote' forgets three-wheeled mopeds.

sceneParams.caption: Mopeds can have 3 wheels too

q18550.en: Pedal-assisted bicycles with an auxiliary electric motor of up to 0.25 kW are defined as mopeds.

explain.short: These e-bikes help only while you pedal, so the law treats them as bicycles, not mopeds.
explain.rule: A ciclomotore (moped) has 2 or 3 wheels, a top speed of 45 km/h and, with a combustion engine, at most 50 cm3. First test after 4 years, then every 2 years.
explain.trap: 'pedalata assistita' (pedal assist) means a bicycle, even with a small motor.

sceneParams.caption: Pedal-assist e-bikes are bicycles, not mopeds

q18551.en: All two-wheeled vehicles with an engine above 50 cm3 are defined as mopeds.

explain.short: It is the opposite: above 50 cm3 a two-wheeler is a motorcycle, not a moped.
explain.rule: A ciclomotore (moped) has 2 or 3 wheels, a top speed of 45 km/h and, with a combustion engine, at most 50 cm3. First test after 4 years, then every 2 years.
explain.trap: 'superiore a 50' (above 50) flips the rule: mopeds are UP TO 50 cm3.

sceneParams.caption: Above 50 cm3 it is a motorcycle

q18552.en: Mopeds, to be defined as such, must have a manual gearbox.

explain.short: The gearbox does not matter: many mopeds are automatic (scooters). Only wheels, engine size and speed count.
explain.rule: A ciclomotore (moped) has 2 or 3 wheels, a top speed of 45 km/h and, with a combustion engine, at most 50 cm3. First test after 4 years, then every 2 years.
explain.trap: 'devono' (must) invents a requirement: the gearbox type is not part of the definition.

sceneParams.caption: Gearbox type doesn't define a moped

q18553.en: Mopeds can travel at 60 km/h outside urban areas.

explain.short: A moped's top speed is 45 km/h everywhere, so 60 km/h is too fast.
explain.rule: A ciclomotore (moped) has 2 or 3 wheels, a top speed of 45 km/h and, with a combustion engine, at most 50 cm3. First test after 4 years, then every 2 years.
explain.trap: '60 km/h' is above the moped limit of 45 km/h, even outside towns.

sceneParams.caption: Mopeds: max 45 km/h, also outside towns

q18554.en: Mopeds are not subject to periodic roadworthiness testing.

explain.short: Mopeds do need the revisione: after 4 years, then every 2 years.
explain.rule: A ciclomotore (moped) has 2 or 3 wheels, a top speed of 45 km/h and, with a combustion engine, at most 50 cm3. First test after 4 years, then every 2 years.
explain.trap: 'non sono soggetti' (are not subject) is wrong: the test is compulsory.

sceneParams.caption: Mopeds DO need periodic tests
